subject.title: feat(tui): add /upload command for file context

question: Should the core TUI own and reserve a built-in `/upload` command that reads local files into the next chat turn, or should file context use an existing Gateway/plugin/file-input boundary first?
rationale: The workflow is useful, but the permanent command namespace and local-file ingestion boundary affect dynamic plugin commands and security behavior, so automation should not choose that direction alone.

options.title: Confirm Core TUI Upload
options.body: Reserve `/upload` for core TUI, then require a rebase plus safety, lifecycle, and collision tests before merge.

options.title: Use Existing File Boundaries
options.body: Pause this branch and ask for a narrower design that reuses Gateway `input_file` or another existing attachment/file-context boundary.

options.title: Defer The Feature
options.body: Leave the feature out of core until a maintainer sponsors local file-context UX across CLI, TUI, and Gateway consistently.

recommendation.title: Confirm Core TUI Upload
recommendation.body: Reserve `/upload` for core TUI, then require a rebase plus safety, lifecycle, and collision tests before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main TUI command and session lifecycle work makes this the clearest routing owner for the command-ownership decision.
